Labour Department announced today (the 10th) that Waso Cafe (Prince Edward) provided false information to the Labour Department during the local open recruitment period when applying for the importation of foreign labour. The department imposed administrative sanctions, including immediately terminating the company's application and refusing to process any applications submitted by the company for the following year. Related report: Importing Foreign Labour｜What were the reasons for administrative sanctions in the 18 cases? Over three years, 1,365 complaints received; about 10% received warnings and administrative sanctions.

Waso Cafe (Prince Edward) was administratively sanctioned by the Labour Department for providing false information during the local open recruitment period.

A spokesperson for the Labour Department stated that after investigation, it was confirmed that Waso Cafe (Prince Edward) had provided false information during the local open recruitment period for importing waiters, junior chefs, and dishwashers, violating the requirements of the Enhanced Supplementary Labour Scheme. Therefore, administrative sanctions were imposed. The department has immediately terminated the company's submitted application for importing foreign labour, and refused to process any applications submitted by the company under the Enhanced Scheme for the following year.

The department emphasised that employers importing foreign labour must strictly comply with the requirements of the scheme, including prioritising the employment of suitable local workers. If employers violate labour or immigration laws, the requirements of the Enhanced Scheme, or the standard employment contract, the Labour Department will impose administrative sanctions, including terminating applications already submitted by the employer, revoking approval already obtained by the employer for importing labour, and refusing to process subsequent applications submitted by the employer.

Including Waso Cafe (Prince Edward), whose sanctions were just announced today, Collective Report (集誌社) has consolidated 18 companies penalised for violating foreign labour importation regulations. Of these, 10 companies belong to the catering services and cleaning industries. What were the reasons for their penalties? Among the 18 companies, 9 were involved in unreasonably refusing to hire local job seekers, with most being refused processing of their foreign labour importation applications for the following two years by the Labour Department. Another two restaurants dismissed local employees after importing foreign labour, and their already-obtained foreign labour approvals were immediately revoked.
